text: A grant unto Joseph Barker, of Regent Street, Lambeth, in the county of Surrey, artist, for his invention of " Improvements in measuring aeriform or fluid substances, "j six months.

A grant unto Witt1AM Henry James, late of Birmingham, but now 1838. of Lambeth, in the county of Surrey, civil engineer, for his invention of ‘Improvements in apparatus for heating, generating, and cooling fluids, and in engines to be actuated by such fluids; parts of which improvements are applicable to the raising and forcing fluids”; 6 months.
A grant unto George Fellows Harrington, of Portsmouth, dentist, for his invention of " Improvements in the manufacture of artificial teeth, and the beds and palates for teeth"; 6 months.

A grant unto John Bevans, of Red Lion Street, Clerkenwell, in the county of Middlesex, joiner, of his new invented method of making circular wooden sash frames, sashes and soffits, fanlights, doors, mouldings, and hand rails for stairs ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & asss, within Engd, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 yrs pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West1", the 4th day of April, in the year above. By writ, &c.
A grant unto John Sylvester, of Great Russell Street, Bloomsbury, in the county of Middlesex, civil engineer, for his invention of "Improvements in stoves and fire places "; 6 months.

A grant unto Morton William Lawrence, of Leman Street, Goodman's Fields, in the county of Middlesex, sugar refiner, for his invented "Improvement in the process of refining sugar"; six mos ; to hold, &c. months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Hooper, of Reading, in the county of Berks, apothecary & man midwife, of the sole use of his new invented medicine comonly called by the name of the female pills ; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assignes, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years according to the statute in that behalf ; and a clause is inserted for obliging him, by a writing under his hand and seal, to cause a particular descripcon of his said invencon to be inrolled in the High Court of Chancery within four kalendar months from the date hereof. Witnesses, John Archbishop of Canterbury, &c, at Westm1", the 21st day of July, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto James Thomson, of Colebrook Terrace, Islington, in the county of Middlesex, merchant, for his invd certain improvements in the construction of fire arms, and the locks to fire arms ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwickupon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date thereof; and U U 2 also with a clause for supplying His Majesty's service with all such articles of the said invention as shall be required by the master general of the ordnance for the time being. By writ, &c.

A grant unto George Thompson, of 12, Park Road, Regent's Park, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for his invention of " Certain improvements in machinery and apparatus for cutting, digging, or turning up earth, applicable to agricultural purposes"; 6 months ; colonies.
A grant unto Charles Heard DE Boissimon, of Leicester Place, in the county of Middlesex, merchant, for "Improvements in manufacturing corks and bungs "; being a communication ; 6 months.
A grant unto John Wiiitehouse the younger, of Birchall Street, Birmingham, brass founder, for his invention of " Improvements in the construction of spring hinges and door springs "j 6 months.

A grant unto John Sutherland, of Liverpool, in the county of Lancaster, copper smith, for his invented improvement in the construction of copper and iron sugar pans and sugar boilers, and a new method of hanging the same ; as also an improvement in the construction of the furnaces or fire places in which such pans and boilers ought to be placed ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute, and also in all our colonies and plantations abroad ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Henry Wright, of the parish of S* Michael's, in the city of London, chymist, of his new invented medicine, which he calls caryophilious regius or royal clove drops ; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westm1, the 11th day of Decr, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Thomas Burstall, of Lee Crescent, Edgbaston, iu the county of Warwick, civil engineer, for his invention of "Certain improved machinery for manufacturing bricks and oilier articles from clay, alone or mixed with other materials"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto William Winlaw, of Margaret Street, Cavendish Square, in the county of Middlesex, engine maker, of his new invented mill for separating the grains from the ears of corn, which has not only been found to perform as much in one hour as can be done by threshing in a day, but likewise to produce a greater quantity of grain, as it will not admit a single grain to remain in the ear, which will be a saving to the public of (at least) as much seed as is sown throughout the whole kingdom ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 21st day of June, in the year above. By writ, &c. s

A grant unto Robert Winch, of Shoe Lane, in the city of London, press maker, for his invtd " Certain improvements on machines or presses, chiefly applicable to printing "; to hold, &c ; four calendar months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Andrew Smith, of Princes Street, in the parish of Saint Martin-in-the-Fields and county of Middlesex, engineer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in engines for exerting power for driving machinery and for raising and lowering heavy bodies 6 months.

A grant unto Robert Hendrick Goddard, of Woolwich, in the county of Kent, gentleman, for his invention of "Certain improvements in the construction of weighing machines, and in the mode, manner, or method of ascertaining, registering, and indicating the number of operations or quantity of work performed by weighing, measuring, or numbering apparatus or machines"; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Thomas Loud, of Hoxton, in the parish of S1 Leonard, Shoreditch, in the county of Middlesex, musical instrument maker, for his new invented improvements in the action and construction of upright pianofortes; to hold to him, his exors, adinors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westm1", the 9th day of March, in the year above. By writ, &r.

A grant unto ALFRED Vincent NEwrTon, of Chancery Lane, in the 1848. | county of Middlesex, mechanical draughtsman, for “Certain improvements in the manufacture of steel”; being a communication ; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Robert John Stanley, of the town of Gainsborough, in the county of Lincoln, gent., for his invented new method of tanning leather without the use or application of bark (or mineral astringent), except in the tanning of backs and bins ; yielding a great advantage, both in respect of time and expence ; whereby as good, if not a superior article or commodity is produced; that the ingredients required by this method of tanning are entirely of a vegetable quality, and the principal part thereof the produce of the united kingdom ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Charles Mepham Hannington, of Nelson Square, in the county of Surrey, gentleman, for his invented " An improved apparatus for impressing, stamping, or printing, for certain purposes"; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Tebaldo Monzani, of Old Bond Street, in the coy of Middx, musical instrument maker, for his invented certain improvements on clarinets and German flutes ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John George, of Chancery Lane, in the county of Middlesex, esq., barrister at law, for his made, found out, or discovered " An invention for preserving decked ships or vessels, so as to render them less liable to dry rot, and for preserving goods on board such ships and vessels from damage by heat"; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto his Grace the Duke of Albemarle, his execs & assignes, of the sole use or exercise of a certaine invencon of saw mills or engines for cleareing of timber of from ye ground in any places within ye collonies or plantacons in America (except New England) for ye terme of 14 yeares according to ye statute in y* case provided ; with other clauses usuall. T. I£ apud Westm, 23 die August, 3tio Jac 2d. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Nathan Waddington, of Hulme, in the county of Lancaster, engineer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the construction of steam boilers, and furnaces for heating the same"; six months.

A grant unto John George Bodmer, of Manchester, in the county of Lancaster, engineer, for his invention of "Certain improvements in the manufacture of metallic hoops and tyres for wheels, and in the method of fixing the same for use; and also improvements in the machinery or apparatus to be employed therein"; 6 months.
A grant unto Cornelius Alfred Jaquin, of Huggin Lane, Wood Street, in the city of London, for his invention of " Improvements in the manufacturer of buttons "; 6 months.

A grant unto Charles William Fenillade, of Mortimer Street, Cavendish Square, in the parish of Saint Mary-le-bone, in the county of Middlesex, gent., for his invented t£ Improved mechanical apparatus, instrument, or machine (intended by him to be called 4 an aid form ') for the prevention and remedy of deformity and ill shape in the trunk or body parts of human beings"; to hold to him, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto GkorGE FrepErick Mountz, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, roller of metals, for his invention of “An improved manufacture of boilers used for the purpose of generating steam ”; six months. By writ, &«.

A grant unto James Mather the younger, of Crow Oaks, Pilkington, in the county of Lancaster, bleacher, and Thomas Edmeston, of the same place, calenderman, for their invention of " Certain improvements in machinery or apparatus for scouring, finishing, and stretching woollen, cotton, and other woven fabrics "; 6 months.

A grant unto Paul Slade Knight, of Lancaster Moor, in the county palatine of Lancaster, gentleman, for his invented " New and improved kind of fire engines, pumps, or other engines, in which are used pistons working in barrels or cylinders"; to hold, &c ; 2 mos. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Samuel Stocker, of the city of Bristol, machinist, for his invention of "Improvements in chimneys for dwelling houses, and in apparatus for scraping, sweeping, or cleaning chimneys, and in the manufacture of such apparatus, and of the materials of which such chimneys are formed 6 months.

A grant unto Wuirinc Haypen, of Windham, in the state of Connecticut, of the United States of America, for his invention of “An improved regulator or apparatus for regulating the draft of the sliver on tne machine termed ‘the drawing frame’”; 6 months. 5158
A grant unto Joseph Clarke, of Boston, in the county of Lincoln, printer, for his invention of " Improvements in pianofortes "; 6 months.

A grant unto Sutton Thomas Wood, of the city of Oxford, brewer, of his new invented improvements on the steam engine, and also the method of adapting and connecting the coppers or boilers, employed in the operation and for the purposes of brewing, to any engine or engines that are worked by the powers of steam & air, so as to render the steam produced from the boiling worts, & the steam produced during the operation of brewing, capable of working those engines commonly known by the name of lire or steam engines ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & asss, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westrnr, the 20th day of Aug*, in the year. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Peter Armand Le Comte de Fontaine Moreau, of 24, Boulevard Poissonniere, Paris, in France, and 4, South Street, Finsburv, London, patent agent, for " Certain improvements in mills for grinding wheat and other grain "; a communication ; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Francis Riciuman, of Great Pulteney Street, Golden Square, in the county of Middlesex, carpenter, for his invented " Certain improvements in the construction of fire escapes, parts of which said improvements are likewise applicable to other purposes "; to hold, &c; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto James Tate, of Mill Street, in the parish of Saint George, Hanover Square, brazier and ironmonger, of his new invented candlesticks, and nozles for sconces, chandeliers, girandoles, & other things used for holding candles, which will receive, keep upright, and hold fast candles of every size without the trouble of paring or the addition of paper, & without damaging the candles, either in putting in or taking out ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon- Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 26th day of Febry, in the year above. By writ, &c.
A grant unto WitiiAM HENSMAN, of Woburn, in the county of Bedford, machinist, for his invention o f “Improvements in ploughs”; 6 months.

A grant unto Robertson Buchanan, engineer, and overseer or manager of the Cotton Milns of Rothsay, in the island of Bute, in that part of Great Britain called Scotland, of his new invented pump, upon an improved construction, for raising water in various situations, but more particularly on board ships, and which may occasionally be converted into an engine for extinguishing of fire ; is not liable to choak or go out of repair, being so constructed as to prevent gravel, dirt, or other things from causing an unnecessary tear and wear of the parts or from lodging in it; and having its valves so situated as to be within the command of a person's hand without taking any part of it asunder; may be worked by any of the methods practised in working the common pump, and is capable of raising a greater quantity of water, with an equal given force, than any other machine for the purpose hitherto invented; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date hereof; and also, if the said Robertson Buchanan, his exors, admors, or assigns, shall not enter into such bond, obligation, or recognizance, in such form and manner, in such words, and under such penalty, as he or they shall at any time during the said term of 14 years be required to enter into by His Majesty's attorney and solicitor general for the time being, or one of them, for the supplying or causing to be supplied His Majesty's ships and vessels, or any of them, with the said invention or any part thereof (if he or they shall be thereto required) in such manner and at and upon such reasonable price and terms as shall be prescribed in and by such bond, obligation, or recognizance; and also, if the said Robertson Buchanan, his exors, admors, and asss, shall not well and truly do, perform, and execute all and singr the condIls, provisoes, covts, and agreemts to be expressed in such bond, oblig", or recognizance, so to be entd into as afsd, that then the sd grant and all liberties and advants whatsr thereby granted shall utterly cease, determe, and become void. W. H. M. at Westm1', the 8th day of March, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Vickers, of Sheffield, in the county of York, merchant, for his invention of " Improvements in machinery for preparing or shaping steel for the manufacture of files and rasps "; two months.

A grant unto Nathaniel Merriman, of Crutched Friars, in the city of London, tin manufacturer, for his new invented stove, grate, or range, upon an improved construction, the improvement of which is likewise applicable to those already in use for the purpose of clearing away foul air from churches, chapels, and all other places of public resort, as well as houses, builds9, and rooms of every description, which he conceives will be of public utility ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England and Wales and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar mouth from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Obed Blake, of the Thames Plate Glass Company, residing at 13, Southampton Street, Strand, gentleman, for his invention of "Certain improvements in ventilating or ventilators for or in ships, vehicles, houses, or other buildings"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Joseph Bramah, of Piccadilly, in the county of Middlesex, engine maker, and Thomas Dickinson, of Bed worth Close, in the county of Warwick, gentleman, of their sundry improvements on an engine or machine originally invented by the said Joseph Bramah, in which said engine or machine may be employed the power or force of steam, condensed air, descents of water, or any other elastic or gravitating fluid, for the purpose of working mills, pumps, and engines or machines of every sort where inanimate power can or may be properly applied to give them motion, and that their said invention, Avhen a power is applied to the center or axis to give it motion, is a compleat engine or machine for raising, pumping, or forcing in any direction air, water, or any other fluid to any given height or distance ; and that the said machine or engine is constructed on a rotative principle, or, in other words, an engine or machine, the motion of which is performed round a center or axis in a rotative, revolving, or circulating direction ; to hold to them, their exors, admors, & asss, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West"", the 15th day of January, in the year of our Lord 1790. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Oldham, of the city of Dublin, gent., for his invtrt or found out " Certain impru in the construction of wheels designed for driving machinery, which are to be impelled by water or by wind ; and which said improvements are also applicable to propelling boats and other vessels "; to hold, fcF ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Ridgway, of Northwood, in the borough of Stoke-upon-Trent, in the county of Stafford, earthenware manufacturer, for his invention of "A new method of conveying and distributing heat in ovens used by manufacturer* of china and earthenware, and brick, tile, and quarry makers "; 6 months.
A grant unto Isham Baggs, of Cheltenham, gentleman, for his invention of " Improvements in engraving, which improvements are applicable to lithography "; 6 months.

A grant unto John Manton, of Davies Street, Piccadilly, in the coy of Middlesex, gun maker, for his invented improvem1 in the construction of hammers and pans to the locks of all kinds of fowling pieces and fire arms ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 2 calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Robertson, of Great Charlotte Street, Buckingham Gate, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for his invention of " Improvements of architecture in its forms and combinations ; and also in the superficial figures which may be employed ; also for an improvement or improvements in the surfaces of buildings "; 6 months.

A grant unto Thomas Martin and Charles Grafton, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, printing ink manufacturers and partners in trade, for their invented " New method of making fine light black of verysuperior colour, which, for distinction from other blacks, they call 'spirit black'; and a new apparatus for producing the same"; two months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Christoph Dihl, of Brewers Street, Golden Sqr, in the coy of Middx, esq1", for his invented method or means of making a mastic cement or composition, which he denominates Dihls mastic ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within fifteen calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Betts, of No. 7, Smithfield Bars, in the city of London, distiller, for his invention of " A new manufacture of capsules, and of a material to be employed therein and for other purposes"; 6 months.
A grant unto Moses Poole, of Lincoln's Inn, in the county of Middlesex, gentn, for "Improvements in the construction of locks"; being a communication ; 6 months.

A grant unto Joseph Jacob the younger, of Saint Mary Axce, London, coachmaker, of his new invented method for ornamenting all sorts of carriages, sedan chairs, buildings, furniture, musical instruments, books and toys ; to hold to him, his exors, adrhors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westm1-, the 14th day of February, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto George Augustus Huddart, of Brynkir, in the county of Caernarvon, esquire, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the manufacture of cigars, and certain improved apparatus lor smoking cigars"; 6 months.
A grant unto Alfred Charles Hobbs, of New York, in the United States of America, engineer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the construction of locks and other fastenings"; 6 months.

A grant unto Josiah Longmore, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, gun lock maker, for his new invented patten or clog ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same Avithin one calendar month from the date thereof. W. II. M. at Westmr, the 2d day of June, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto James Murphy, of Hertford Street, in the parish of Sl Pancras, in the county of Middlesex, of his new invented improvements in the art of tanning all manner of hides and skins, and in the construction of tan pits or vats, with several utensils appertaining to the same ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, Within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within six calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 27th day of Janry, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Bell, of Edinburgh, in that part of our united kingdom called Scotland, writer to our signet, for his invented certain improvements in the apparatus for copying manuscripts or other writings or designs ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Henry Hina Epwarps, of Nottingham Terrace, New Road, in the county of Middlesex, engineer, for his invention of « Improvements in evaporation ”; 6 months. s6s0. A grant unto Pierre Marurw Mannoury, of Paris, but now of Leicester Square, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for “ Improvements in wind and string musical instruments ”; being a communication ; 6 months.
A grant unto Louis Prosper Nicolas Duval Piron, of Paris, engineer, for " Certain improvements in tubes, pipes, flags, curbs for pavement, and tram roads "; 6 months ; colonies.
A grant unto Thomas Halahan, of York Street, Dublin, lieutenant in the royal navy, for his invented "Machinery or apparatus for working ordnance "; to hold, &t: ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Pierre Armand Le Comte he Fontainemoreau, of South Street, Finsbury, London, patent agent, for " Certain hygienic apparatus and processes for preventing and curing chronical and other affections, and to prevent or stop certain epidemic diseases "; being a communication ; 6 months ; colonies.

A spiall priviledge graunted to George Manby and Thomas Lidell, and their assignes, for the terme of xiiij yeares next ensuing, to practise and | putt in use within England, Ireland, and Wales the sole makinge, tryminge, B 4< selling, and putting out to liire of a new forme of mills for the grindinge of cornc, &c, not formerly used in this kingdome, whereof the said George Manby is the true inventor — paying therefore yearely into the exeheq1* xiij1' vjs viijd; prohibiting all others to doe the like ; with the ordinary proviso to make this grant voide in ease it shal be found piudiciall. Teste apud Westm1", xxvj° Novembf, anno pd. p bfe &c.

A grant unto Charles Random Baron De Berenger, of Target Cottage, Kentish Town, in the parish of Sl Pancras and county of Middx, for his discovered and invented " Certain improvements in gun powder flasks, powder horns, or other utensils of different shapes, such as are used or can be used for the purpose of carrying gunpowder therein, in order to load therefrom guns, pistols, blunderbusses and other fire arms"; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Robert Eaton, dr in physick, his execrs, admrs, & assignes, of the sole use & benefit of his new invented chymical pparaton & styptick medicine, void of all corrosive qualities, being both cordial and balsamick, which universally stops all external and internal bleedings, & of itsselfe heals all fresh wounds, & vastly exceeds all other stypticks that ever were prepared in England, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon- Tweed according to the statute in such case made & provided. Teste, &<', ut supra. p bre, &c.

A grant unto George Ambroise Michaut, of Epieds, in the kingdom of France, now residing at New Bond Street, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for his invention of " Improvements in the production and application of heat, and in the manufacture of coke"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto FrepEericK CoLiieR BAKEWELL, of Hampstead, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for his invention of “ Certain improvements in machinery or apparatus for making or manufacturing soda water and other aerated waters and liquids”; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Joun Barron, deputy comptroller of our Mint, for his invented “Certain process for the application of the prismatic colours to the surface of steel and other metals, and using the same in the manufacture of various ornaments”; to hold, &°; two months. By writ, &¢.

A grant unto John Bowler, of Nelson Sq., Blackfriars Road, in the coy of Surrey, and Thomas Galon, of the Strand, in the coy of Middx, hat manufacturers, for their invented " Certain imprts in the construction or manufacture of hats"; to hold, &c ; six mos. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Lester, of Paddington Green, in the parish of Paddington, in the county of Middx, engineer, for his invented various further improvements on an engine or machine for separating corn seeds and pulse from the straw and chaff, and for wch said engine or machine the said W. Lester obtained His Majesty's Letters Patent, dated 16th Janry 1805 ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within six calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Joe Sidebottom, of Pendlebury, in the county of Lancaster, manager, for his invention of " Certain improvements in steam engines"; 6 months.
A grant unto William Grtsenthavaite, of Kings Place, Nottingham, gentleman, for his invented "Improvement in air engines"; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &(;.

A grant unto Augustus Applegath, of Crayford, in the county of Kent, calico printer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in letter press and block printing, and in the machinery or apparatus used for the same"; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Erastus B. Bigelow, of Boston, in the state of Massachusetts, in the United States of America, for his invention of " Certain new and useful improvements in looms for weaving certain kinds of carpets or other fabrics of like character"; 6 months.

A grant unto John Cockshutt, of Wortley Ironworks, in the county of York, ironmaster, of his new invented art of making malleable iron directly from the ore, with sea coals or pit coals in a finery or bloomery, without pursuing those tedious and expensive methods now in practice for the making of iron ; and also of his new invented method of refining sow, pig, or cast iron with charcoal into wrought or bar iron, so as to perforin the same better and with much greater expedition and less consumption of charcoal than can be done by any other method now or heretofore known and practiced ; and also of his new invented finery or bloomery for the making and refining of iron, much better adapted for the purpose than those which now are or have at any time been in use in these kingdoms ; to hold to him, his exors, adrhors, and assigns, within England, Wales, the town of Berwickupon-Tweed, and all the colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 2nd day of May, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Richter of his new invented art or method of inlaying scaglialier or plaister upon marble and metals to imitate flowers, birds, &c ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at W., the 28th day of Decr, 1770. By writ, &c.

snuffboxes of a new invention ; a pen knife yt make ye pen at one cut ; a pocket knife of a new contrivance ; & buckles wthout anchors, wth a folding tongue ; a machine wth moving circles, ten, faces on each, with nine figures & a cypher thereon described, usefull in drawing lotterys & other matters of public use ; two case of pistols, of which a carbine may be made & charged wthout a rammer ; a turning mattress fit for armies & hospitals, coaches and chaises, that can neither overturn nor jolt ; a method to prevent shipwreck ; a bomb or granado that will burst at ye proper distance, & not discover its way in the air ; brest plates full proof, lighter by half than ordinary ; candlesticks & rings to be made wider or straighter as occasion ; sharp pointed scissars to be carryed in ye pocket wlhout any case or danger ; a coin odious machine, on wch to place a bottle or two & glasses at table ; a picture yl serves for a tester to a couch bed in ye night, & is put up again in the day time for an ornament to a room ; a lanthorn into which a candle may be put with more ease than into those now used ; a lock of a fuzil more plain & solid than ordinary ; a means to fire the fuzil always horizontally ; & double counters, with a number upon each for the fair drawing of lotterys ; to hold & exercise the same within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for & during the term of 14 years according to the statute in such case made and provided. Teste ^ apd Westm, 12° die Augst, anno pd. p bre, &c.
